Install Cookie Compliance on your platform

View raw markdown (for agents)

In short: the banner is one two-tag snippet that works on any website whose code you can edit, whatever it is built with. What changes from platform to platform is where the snippet goes. Find your platform below for the exact spot, or use the general steps if it isn't listed.

The one rule #

Blocking works by execution order, and code that has already run cannot be un-run. So the snippet must be the first script on every page, in <head>, as plain synchronous tags (no async, defer or type="module"), above analytics, pixels and any tag manager.

Platforms with a guide #

Each guide covers the wrong way, the right way, and how to check that it worked.

Platform Where the snippet goes Guide
WordPress Install the Cookie Compliance for WordPress plugin; do not paste the snippet into a theme wordpress
Shopify First thing in <head> of layout/theme.liquid, not checkout Additional scripts or a Customer Events pixel shopify
Next.js The document <head> of the root layout, as classic tags (not next/script) nextjs
Nuxt app.head.script in nuxt.config.ts, never marked async nuxt
Astro The shared layout's <head>, with is:inline on every tag astro
Angular <head> of src/index.html, not the angular.json scripts array angular
React or Vue (Vite) <head> of index.html, ahead of the module entry vite
SvelteKit src/app.html, above %sveltekit.head% sveltekit
Google Tag Manager <head>, above the GTM container; never as a tag inside GTM gtm
Static HTML or any other site you edit directly First thing in <head> on every page (or the shared header file) plain-html

Your platform isn't listed #

If you can put code in the <head> of every page, the plain HTML steps apply:

  1. Copy the live snippet from the dashboard (Integrations → Manual Integration), or with the MCP server connected call install.getSnippet. Paste it unchanged. No account yet? Sign up (free plan, no card).
  2. Paste it as the first thing inside <head>, on every page or in the shared header your pages include.
  3. Check it with verify-install: before the visitor chooses, no tracking cookies should appear.

If your platform only offers a footer or <body> code box, or places custom code after its own scripts, the snippet will run after your trackers and cannot hold them. Say so rather than installing it there, and use a spot that comes first. The checks in verify-install show whether it held.
